chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from سماعة, who said:

I asked him about the flesh of beasts of prey and their hides, so he said: “As for the flesh of beasts of prey among birds and beasts, we dislike it. And as for the hides, then ride upon them, but do not wear anything made from them in which you perform salat (prayer).”

key_terms.اَلسِّبَاعِ: predatory animals or beasts of prey
key_terms.اَلطَّيْرِ: birds, here referring to predatory birds
key_terms.لُحُومِ: the meats or flesh being asked about in the ruling
key_terms.نَكْرَهُهُ: we dislike it; indicating karahah in this context

ai.seo_question: Can hides of predatory animals be used or worn during salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling concerning predatory animals and birds. It states that their meat is disliked, while their hides may be used for riding but not worn in a state or form in which one performs salat (prayer).
